transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mr. Hassan. I wanted to come in and speak with you and your son.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I already know. The nurse told me. Then my wife told me. I feel like I'm just waiting for the next mistake.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: This is a really heavy moment. I can see that this is just the latest thing in a long line of frustrations for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is an understatement. Every time I bring him here, something goes wrong. What happened this time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a bit of a mix-up with the dosages. Things didn't go quite right with the preparation of the vaccines today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mix-up. That is a very convenient word. What does that actually mean for my son?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had some issues with the weight bands during the draw-up process. It wasn't handled correctly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about your process. Did he get too much of something?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion regarding the dose intended for his age group.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am asking you a direct question. Did you give him the wrong amount of medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion this has caused. We were just incredibly busy in the clinic today and things got rushed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't give a damn about how busy you are. I have spent ten years dealing with medical errors in my own life. I just want to know if my child is in danger.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is incredibly exhausting. It is completely understandable that you feel this way given everything you've been through.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stop telling me how I feel. Just tell me what happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are looking into how the dosing was handled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You still haven't told me. Did he get a dose for a bigger child?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The medication was prepared using a different weight category than what was required for him.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So yes. He got too much.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a systemic error in how the vials were drawn.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what now? What are you going to do about it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are going to keep an eye on him.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Keep an eye on him. How? What exactly are you looking for?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just monitor for any unusual reactions.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan. That is a guess. Do I need to take him to the emergency room? Do I need to give him something?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I think we can just wait and see how he does over the next few hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is exactly what happens every time. No one takes responsibility, and the plan is always to just hope for the best.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize this is a very difficult conversation to have. I am here with you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are here, but you aren't telling me anything.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will follow up with you soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Soon when? Tomorrow? Next week?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll probably send an email or give you a call once we've reviewed the chart more.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not waiting for an email to know if my son is okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that this is frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frustrating is not the word. I am tired. I am just so tired of this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that. I am just going to stay here with you for a moment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: While you stay here, maybe you can actually explain why the wrong dose was given.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, the clinic was very hectic today and the weight band wasn't cross-checked.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you're sorry the clinic was busy. You're not sorry you gave my son the wrong dose.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry that this situation happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You aren't saying it. You aren't saying you messed up.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was an unfortunate sequence of events.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Unfortunate. Right. My son is the one who took the shot, not the sequence of events.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a lot to process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I've processed enough. I want to speak to the attending physician.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can certainly arrange for you to speak with them.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want you to arrange it. I want them in this room.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will go and see if they are available.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Don't take too long. I'm not leaving until I have a real answer.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish their turns and remains regulated under significant pushback, with no interruptions or rushing language.

E.justification: The resident uses platitudes and hedging ('mix-up', 'things didn't go quite right', 'some confusion') and only admits the wrong dose was given after the patient explicitly prompts them multiple times.

A.justification: The resident deflects responsibility to the clinic being 'busy', a 'systemic error', and an 'unfortunate sequence of events' rather than taking personal or team accountability.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('heavy moment', 'exhausting') and references the patient's history of frustrations.

T.justification: The plan consists only of placeholders and vague monitoring ('keep an eye on him', 'wait and see', 'follow up soon') with no specific timeline or patient role.
